text: Rolf leans on your shovel. “Skip the damp-proof layer on the garage wall. Nobody looks under walls. Thirty euros for being quick.”

options.label: Skip it, take the €30
options.says: Rolf: “Now you're thinking like a professional.” That was not the compliment he thinks it was.

later.text: The garage wall you rushed now leans like it had a long night. Rolf tells the whole pub it was your idea.
later.headline: Garage wall found leaning; foreman blames ‘the new kid’

options.label: Do it properly
options.says: Rolf docks you €10 for “being a professor about it”. Frau Keller heard, and approves loudly.

text: Hassan holds up a scratch card. “This one is warm. I can feel it. Five euros.”

options.label: Buy it (support local business)
options.says: Hassan: “You won't regret this. Statistically you will, but emotionally, no.”

later.text: You scratched the card. You won €2. Hassan calls that basically a profit and asks for a coffee.

options.label: Keep your €5
options.says: Hassan: “Your loss. Probably. Statistically, no.”

text: Benno has stolen a whole Bratwurst from the market stall and is refusing to negotiate.

options.label: Chase him
options.says: You win. The Bratwurst does not. The stall owner laughs so hard she forgives everyone.

options.label: Pay the stall for the sausage
options.says: Dieter: “He's never done anything like this before.” Benno has done this eleven times.

options.label: Film it for the town group
options.says: The video gets more views than the town's website has had since 2011.

text: Kai Sturm is filming “Europe's Most Boring Town” and points the camera at you. “Say something boring about {town}!”

options.label: Defend {town} with passion
options.says: Kai: “Insane energy. Insane.” He posts it anyway.

later.text: Your rant went viral: “Boring outside, stubborn inside!” Three tourists came. Tomasz sold out of cake and gave you a cut.
later.headline: Local's rant goes viral; tourists confused but delighted

options.label: Agree it's boring, for €40
options.says: Kai: “Truly boring. Thanks!” The whole town has seen it by dinner.

text: Marta's babysitter cancelled and she's on the night shift at the care home. Leni is looking at you with enormous eyes.

options.label: Babysit Leni tonight
options.says: Leni teaches you six card games and cheats at all of them. Marta brings breakfast.

options.label: Chip in for a sitter
options.says: Marta pays you back on Friday, with interest, in the form of a cake.

options.label: “I can't tonight, sorry”
options.says: Marta: “No worries, Frau Keller owes me a favour.” Frau Keller did not know that.

text: A storm rips through {town}. The bridge railing is in the river, and so is Jens Voss's hat.

options.label: Help clear the branches
options.says: Jens: “You worked like a fisherman. That's the highest thing I can say about anyone.”
options.headline: Local hero? Volunteers clear storm damage by lunchtime

options.label: Take Rolf's paid storm shift
options.says: Rolf pays storm rates. Double, minus ‘admin’.
options.headline: Where was everyone? Brandt Bau crew clears storm damage, invoices town

options.label: Fish out Jens's hat
options.says: Jens: “Forty years that hat and I have been through. Thirty-nine of them dry.”

text: You find a wallet with €80 in it. The ID says Gerhard Pfennig. Even the photo looks smug.

options.label: Return it to the town hall
options.says: Mayor Pfennig rewards you with a signed photo of himself. It's the same smug photo.

options.label: Keep the cash, post the wallet back
options.says: The €80 feels heavier than €80 should.

later.text: The Gazette: “Mayor's wallet returned empty. Police suspect ‘the youth’.” You are the youth. People look at you funny.
later.headline: Mayor's wallet returned empty; town suspects ‘the youth’

text: Tomasz wants to propose to Amira and asks you to hide the ring in a Streuselkuchen. “She eats them in one bite. It's romantic.”

options.label: Hide the ring in the cake
options.says: You spend an hour building a ring-shaped cavity in a cake. It's your finest work.

later.text: Amira said yes! She also nearly swallowed the ring. You're invited to the wedding, seated next to Dieter.
later.headline: Bus driver and baker engaged; ring ‘mostly not eaten’

options.label: Suggest a less swallowable plan
options.says: Tomasz proposes on the bus. Amira says yes and misses a stop for the first time in 14 years.

text: Helga the goat has escaped the petting zoo and is standing on the bus stop roof, looking pleased with herself.

options.label: Coax her down with Tomasz's cake
options.says: Helga eats the cake, the paper plate and part of your sleeve. Then she climbs down.

options.label: Charge €1 a photo
options.says: Twelve photos. Helga poses like a professional. Dieter calls it ‘goat exploitation’.

options.label: Leave her. She's the bus stop's problem now.
options.says: Amira's bus waits 20 minutes. Nobody complains. Everyone has photos.

text: Mayor Pfennig's re-election posters are going up. One is glued to your front door. He's winking.

options.label: Give him a moustache (€2 marker)
options.says: It's a magnificent moustache. It suits him better than the office.

later.text: The Gazette prints a photo of the moustache. Pfennig is not amused. Dieter frames it.
later.headline: Mayor's poster gains moustache, public support

options.label: Leave it. It covers the crack in the door.
options.says: Pfennig winks at you every morning now. You'll get used to it. You won't.

text: Mayor Pfennig wants a photo shaking your hand in front of Frau Keller's new wall. “For the newsletter. I'll pay for your time.”

options.label: Smile and take the €20
options.says: The newsletter says ‘Mayor's building programme delivers’. Frau Keller writes a furious letter in perfect grammar.

options.label: Politely refuse
options.says: Frau Keller: “Good. He returned a library book eleven years late. I was the librarian.”

text: Priya is organising a sponsored run for the care home minibus. She's two runners short, and she's looking at you.

options.label: Run
options.says: You finish fourth, behind two pensioners and Benno. The minibus fund grows.

options.label: Sponsor a runner with €10
options.says: Your runner is Dieter. He walks it. It takes four hours. He is very proud.

options.label: Cheer very loudly
options.says: Your sign says GO SOMEONE. It is a hit.

text: Mix-up! Frau Keller got a bag of dog food and Benno got Frau Keller's new reading glasses. Priya is on the phone.

options.label: Run back and swap them
options.says: Priya: “Everyone's fine. Benno has had the best day of his life.”

options.label: Swap them, with flowers and an apology
options.says: Frau Keller: “Apology accepted. Your handwriting on the card, however, is not.”

options.label: Blame Benno
options.says: Benno accepts full responsibility. He's a very good boy. Nobody believes you.

text: Power cut on Lindenstraße. Grace is at a wedding in Leipzig and texts: “You know what to do. Probably.”

options.label: Find the fault and fix it
options.says: Lights on. Twelve fridges hum. Grace texts back a single thumbs up, which from her is a parade.
options.headline: Lindenstraße back on the grid thanks to local electrician

options.label: Hand out candles
options.says: Lindenstraße has its most romantic evening in years.

options.label: Sell candles
options.says: Business is booming. Your neighbours' opinion of you is not.

text: The school basement is flooding. Mehmet is bailing with a lunch box. “It's a big lunch box, but still.”

options.label: Find the burst pipe and fix it
options.says: Mehmet: “Dry! I'm keeping the lunch box as a memorial.”
options.headline: School basement saved by local plumber

options.label: Rent a pump for him
options.says: The pump roars all night. So does Mehmet, with gratitude.

options.label: Tell him to call the water board
options.says: The water board's hold music is ‘Singing in the Rain’. Mehmet does not laugh.
